description: Production security hardening - Secure docker-compose configuration, harden CORS policy, add resource limits, implement secure secrets management pattern, and add security headers middleware to FastAPI.
steps: Update docker-compose.yml: Remove hardcoded postgres password 'postgres', use ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-change_me_in_production} environment variable for postgres service
Update docker-compose.yml: Remove hardcoded MinIO credentials, use ${MINIO_ROOT_USER} and ${MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD} environment variables
Update docker-compose.yml: Add resource limits to all services (backend: memory 512M, celery_worker: memory 256M, frontend: memory 256M, postgres: memory 1G, redis: memory 256M)
Update docker-compose.yml: Add restart policies 'unless-stopped' to all services
Update backend/app/core/config.py: Change ALLOWED_ORIGINS field_validator to reject overly permissive regex in production - only allow exact domain matches when APP_ENV=production
Create backend/app/core/security.py with security headers middleware implementing HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, X-XSS-Protection, CSP headers
Add security headers middleware to backend/main.py after CORS middleware
Create .env.example files in backend/ and frontend/ with placeholder values and clear comments (never commit actual .env)
Update backend/README.md with section on secrets management: explain environment variables, .env.example usage, production secrets via AWS Secrets Manager or similar
Create backend/tests/test_security_hardening.py testing: CORS rejects unauthorized origins in production mode, security headers present in responses, resource limits applied to containers
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.yml uses environment variables for all sensitive credentials (no hardcoded passwords)
All Docker services have memory and CPU limits defined
All Docker services have restart: unless-stopped policy
CORS configuration rejects unauthorized origins when APP_ENV=production
Security headers middleware adds 5+ security headers to all responses
verification: docker compose config (parses successfully with environment variable substitution)
grep -r 'postgres:postgres@' docker-compose.yml (returns no matches - no hardcoded passwords)
docker compose up -d (all services start with resource limits)
docker stats (shows memory limits enforced on containers)
Set APP_ENV=production in backend/.env and restart backend, verify CORS rejects localhost origin
